Bowhunter Cameron Hanes returns to Joe Rogan for episode 2514. Hanes pairs daily hard training with deep backcountry hunts. His motto, keep hammering, drives a loyal fan base.

The pair swap tales from hunts in rough, high country. Hanes explains why effort matters more than gear or luck. Rogan shares his own respect for that grind. The episode is rugged and plain spoken. It suits hunters and anyone who draws drive from a man who treats each dawn run as a duty, not a choice. Discipline, not talent, is his constant theme.
uslaw-usc-t2-s190m:
Section 190m of Title 2 of the United States Code deals with subpoenas for taking testimony in congressional matters. It sits in a chapter on congressional and committee procedure and investigations. Depositions taken away from the chamber need officers to serve papers and run the taking of evidence.

The section makes the local United States marshal serve subpoenas issued for the United States. He serves them in the same manner as subpoenas from his district court. Subpoenas issued for a private party are served after his fees are first paid. The presiding master may also appoint another person to serve a subpoena. The master holds full power to swear witnesses under oath. He may also issue attachments to force witnesses to attend and to bring papers with them. The head of the section shows the legal plumbing behind testimony taken for Congress outside its own rooms.
